plan.encoder: 145 private observation values: original99 + explicit engine feedback, interaction margins, incoming attacker, own previous executed intent. MLP128/64 GRU64 actor64/9.
plan.recovery_corpus: student-recovery-corpus-v2, eight train seeds only, 500 turns, old99 prior trajectories
plan.training: 30 epochs each, seed2026, validation macroF1 checkpoint, recovery sequence oversampling4
plan.comparison: current teacher vs old99 prior under same new rules vs new135 demos alone vs new135 + on-policy corrections
plan.selection: offline validation only; final fresh-seed comparison run after model selection. No model updates or masks during evaluation.
plan.amendment_before_fresh_evaluation: Include old99 model under matched current rules: correction collection showed old model can reproduce under new healing/cutoff rules. Avoid attributing rule effects to retraining.
plan.secondary_audit: Count unexecutable goals, waiting and waiting hungry with visible food, in addition to engine refusals. Added after 100-turn seed23 training-seed diagnostic showed fewer refusals can mean waiting instead; frozen models unchanged.

fresh_manifest.selection: argmax learned lifecycle logits, no teacher goal fallback; identical motor/engine rules
fresh_manifest.newborns: same learned weights, separate fresh GRU state

limitations: One model initialization per condition; eight descriptive fresh seeds, no significance claim.
Prior vs new models changes both encoder and teacher corpus. Demos vs recovery adds correction data with fourfold sampling and more optimizer steps per epoch; it is not a step-matched ablation.
Corrective labels come from old99 student trajectories, not an iterative rollout of the newly fitted controller.
Own previous intent is causal executed activity, never current teacher answer; all model actions are unmasked argmax.
Shared authored target/motor controllers and engine remain; no trained world-model planner or learned cost in this test.
Different decisions alter event order and random consumption. Aggregate event counts depend on population and lifespan.
Retained-target mismatch counts are a post-hoc failure audit, not a prespecified primary outcome. No model was changed after inspecting fresh failures.
Raw data and weights remain outside Git; no live deployment.
